title: Choose the visual world for the study site
question: The roll assigned the Engineering Computation Pad. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Engineering Computation Pad
options.lineage: Green engineering computation pads and quad-ruled lab notebooks
options.thesis: Every lesson is a numbered sheet of worked computation: title block, ruled grid, every step shown.
materials: grid printed through from the back
options.viewport: A title block across the top (COURSE · LECTURE 01 · SHEET 3 OF 6 · memory and pointers), the left rail as the sheet index, and a calm white reading column laid on the green grid, with a byte diagram drawn on graph cells.
options.risk: If the grid reaches the reading column it becomes a costume; it must stay in the frame and figures.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: a pencil tick for a lesson done, a struck cross for a wrong check, a folded red flag where you stopped.
The red pencil is reserved for wayfinding and state only: where you are, what is next, what you got wrong. Nowhere else.
One 8px baseline unit, shared by the grid, the type, and every figure, so the paper and the text line up.

options.label: Processor Datasheet
options.lineage: 1970s-90s chip databooks and architecture reference manuals
options.thesis: The course as a technical reference manual: numbered sections, register diagrams, ruled tables, one spot colour.
options.viewport: A running head with section number (2.3 Memory and pointers), a thin index rail, the reading column, and a figure set as a bit-field register diagram with numbered bit positions.
options.risk: Closest to what technical documentation already looks like, so it can read as familiar rather than ours.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: film editors' cutting benches and select rails
options.thesis: Each session is a strip of frames on a perforated rail; a folded flag marks where you stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated rail across the top with the session's steps as frames; the current step in a punched white window below.
options.case: Strong for guided sessions and progress; students do not recognise a cutting bench, and a black-and-orange ground is tiring for long reading.
options.risk: Wins the session pages, loses the lesson pages, where reading is the job.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every page is a decision point showing only the way ahead.
options.viewport: A yellow band naming the next step, gate-style lesson numbers.
options.case: Clear wayfinding, but students do not identify with it and the yellow fights long reading.
options.kept: Colour reserved for wayfinding and nothing else.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap text riding baselines over a black void.
options.viewport: A single bitmap line over drifting star fields.
options.case: Fun for programmers, but a bitmap face for running text breaks beginner reading.
options.kept: One shared baseline unit for every element.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack every lesson into ruled modules.
options.viewport: A mosaic of boxed lesson modules.
options.case: Density is the opposite of what a beginner needs.
options.kept: Glossary and reference pages may run denser than lessons.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: Pages ruled as one continuous section.
options.case: Beautiful but unrelated to the subject.
options.risk: Nobody knows why it looks like architecture.
options.kept: Annotations pinned in the margin, beside what they explain.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone labeled with its literal quoted name.
options.viewport: Quoted caps labels and hazard stripes.
options.case: Fashion irony does not match a beginner course.
options.risk: Joke wears thin by lesson two.
options.kept: Labels say literally what a thing is.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean documentation site, like the best course and docs sites, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of lectures and lessons, a centred article column, an on-this-page list on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other docs site by design.
